t.E217.agn: In the body it is assessed in the same way as propyl paraben (E 216). In 2004 EFSA did not include propyl paraben in the group ADI for methyl and ethyl paraben (0–10 mg/kg body weight); no ADI could be proposed because effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs had been reported in young rats and a clear no-effect dose could not be established. E 217 was also removed from the EU list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC.
t.E217.body: Parabens are well absorbed when taken orally and are rapidly broken down in the body (in the liver and kidneys) to p-hydroxybenzoic acid; the ester form can rarely be measured in the blood. This acid is excreted in urine, either free or bound to glycine and glucuronic acid.
t.E217.eff.0.a: No no-effect dose could be established
t.E217.eff.0.t: Effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs were seen in young rats; it was therefore removed from the EU list of additives
t.E217.eval: In the EU it was removed from the list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC (EFSA 2004: no ADI could be proposed for propyl paraben). California AB 418 bans propyl paraben in food from 2027.
t.E217.found.0: Not authorised in food in the EU since 2006
t.E217.prod: A paraben produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E217.regx.0: No ADI could be proposed for propyl paraben and its sodium salt.
t.E217.regx.1: Removed from the 95/2/EC list of additives by Directive 2006/52/EC; not included in the list in Annex II Part B of 1333/2008.
t.E217.regx.2: AB 418 bans propyl paraben (CAS 94-13-3) in food from 1 January 2027; the text of the law does not separately name the sodium salt.
t.E217.summary: A synthetic preservative from the paraben group (an ester of p-hydroxybenzoic acid). Used against moulds and yeasts; more common in cosmetics than in food.
t.E217.what: The sodium salt of propyl paraben; it was used as a preservative against moulds and yeasts and is no longer authorised in the EU.
